title: Option drag on a clip leaves a copy behind
goal: Holding Option while dragging a clip along the timeline should drag out a copy and leave the original where it was, as it does in Premiere, Final Cut and on Photonz's own canvas. Today Option on the timeline only draws a range, so an editor's first reflex for reusing a piece does nothing they expect.
notes: Lane press: TimelineTrackRows.swift:965-990 uses Option to start a range on empty space (drawsRange). Clip bar drag: Sources/PhotonzCore/ClipBarDrag.swift + Sources/Photonz/EditorState+ClipBar.swift have no modifier handling at all (grep option/modifierFlags finds nothing). Option-copy already exists on the canvas and in key lanes; match its cursor. Duplicate (Command J) already exists in the clip menu (EditorState+TimelineMenus.swift:213) for the copy itself. Found by the 2026-10-05 evening manager pass's key audit.
acceptance: Option and drag on a clip's bar moves a copy (with its linked sound) to where you let go, snapping as a plain drag does, and the original stays put; one undo removes the copy
Option and drag on EMPTY track space still draws a range, as today
The pointer shows the copy cursor while Option is held over a clip, the same as the canvas's Option drag
A walk at Next defaults Option-drags a clip to a later moment and checks there are two clips with the same source; it runs green
Try it: open a recording, split it with B, hold Option and drag the second piece to the right. Audit written under queue/audits/
